segments.text: Hello Hannah, come and take a seat. What would you like to talk about today?
I'm not really sure where to start. I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September.
What happened in September?
It was my deputy head at my school
I've taught here for 11 years and I have loved it and then they had asked me to step up and when our deputy left
That sounds like recognition of your work.
That's what everyone says, but I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and
that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.
What does it look like when that dot arrives?
Mostly Sunday evenings.
My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.
What do you rehearse?
Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say then what they would think of me if I got it wrong.
What do you imagine they would think?
That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice earful teacher who can't actually read.
Has anyone said anything that suggests that?
no that's the strange thing
nobody has
it's all in my head
it's so very real to you
very
last week I rewrote the same email
three governors four times
four times
what was the email about
change to the behavior policy
it was two paragraphs
I was afraid Mr.
Hargraves
the chair of governors
would think that I was stupid
How does he treat you?
He has been nothing but kind
He told me in September he was delighted
That makes it worse somehow
Because I feel like I'm lying to him
Lying to him about what?
About being capable
As if I'm pretending
Pretending to be what?
Somebody who knows what she's doing
Most days I feel like a child
Wearing her mother's coat
That's a vivid image. Whose coat is that?
My mum's, I suppose. She was a headteacher for 20 years.
Tell me about that.
She was brilliant. Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.
She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.
Do you know anyone with a similar job?
A deputy's job, but yes.
I can't help comparing.
Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?
Does she say that?
Never. She is very supportive on the surface.
She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.
How does it blend when she says that?
It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss so I don't tell her how bad it is.
What does she not know?
That I'm awake at 4 every morning.
I fall asleep fine then I'm awake at 4 going through the to-do list.
What else is on the list?
Everything. Timetable changes, the offset prep, a parent complained, a child I'm worried about. It goes round and round.
How long have you been waking like that?
Since about the second week of term. I drink a lot of coffee to get through a day which I know doesn't help.
How many cups?
Five or six.
Then I can't sit still in the afternoons.
What do you notice in your body during those afternoons?
My heart goes fast.
My hands are a bit shaky.
Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.
Did anyone notice?
I don't think so.
I said I was fetching a document.
That sounds like a lot of effort to hide it.
It is. I am exhausted by the end of every day, just from pretending.
Who knows how you're feeling?
My partner Ben knows a bit. He says I should just enjoy it.
How do you feel when he says that?
Guilty and a bit alone. He means well. He's an engineer. He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it.
You can't just fix this.
No. I wish it were that simple.
Do you have friends at school you can talk to?
Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year four corridor with the others.
Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.
Say it was some company along with the promotion.
Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that.
I miss them.
I miss my class too.
What do you miss most?
The children mostly.
The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.
No, my days are spreadsheets.
Did you want deeper emotion?
I thought I did
I said yes in the room
Because I couldn't say no to her
The hat
Then I went home and cried
What were the tears about?
Fear I think
And that I would never get to go back
Would you want to go back?
I don't know
That sounds terrible, doesn't it?
After everyone's been so supportive.
That sounds like an honest question.
Nobody has asked me that.
They just say, well done.
When was the last time you felt properly relaxed?
These summer holidays.
We went walking in the lakes.
And I didn't think about school once for ten days.
What was different there?
Nobody expected anything of me. I was just walking, Ben carried the sandwiches.
Uh, yeah?
The week before term I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.
Is there anything you already tried to tell, even let me?
I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things, a chill laughing,
a good email. How did that go?
It held
for about two weeks and then
I stopped because I felt
silly. Silly in what way?
As if I were
bragging to myself
in a notebook.
Noticing what went
well is not the same
as bragging. Probably
not.
It just felt that way.
It sounds worried
back coming to
Have you thought about whether there is something particular you would like from our work?
I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.
What would that look like on a Tuesday?
Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first.
Sending an email once.
And on Sunday?
being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots
those are clear goals how do you feel now saying them out loud
a lightful lighter a bit tearful actually that's all right take a moment sorry i didn't expect that
There is nothing to apologize for. What's coming up?
That's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is.
Not even Ben knows how about the 4am.
What would it be like to tell him?
Scary. He would probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.
Would it be a reason to keep it to yourself?
I suppose not try this week.
What would help you do that?
If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too warmed up.
Saturday morning, perhaps?
Yeah, over breakfast. He's always in a good mood then.
And one more small thing. Would you try the evening notebook again, just for a week? Even one line?
I could. I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget.
We're nearly out of time. Is there anything you want to add?
Only did I nearly cancel this morning. I'm glad I didn't.
and luck to you
same time next week
yes please thank you
